correctness.rationale: With d=1/b and a=1/2, periodization of modulation coefficients gives the Walnut factor 1/b. Exactly two translates contribute to the diagonal; the b<=1 case has no off-diagonal overlaps. When a<d<2a, only shifts +/-d overlap, and the forward shift contributes -1 precisely when the residue t of the starting point lies below a-(d-a). Residues along a fiber advance by d-a mod a; edges are exactly the advances without a wrap. Each component begins at t0 in [0,d-a) and has ceil((a-t0)/(d-a)) vertices. The maximal length L=ceil(a/(d-a)) occurs on an open interval of positive length contained in the direct-integral base [0,d), also when a/(d-a) is an integer. The sine eigenvectors of the finite Dirichlet path give the extreme spectral values on these fibers, so the two bounds are truly optimal. The jumps follow from the one-sided ceiling change, the critical limit from L~2/(2-b), and the b=2 fiber is the bilateral discrete Laplacian divided by 2, with zero spectral infimum. This proof uses no rationality hypothesis.
residual_risks: The archived line 'periodic finite-grid operator spectra' counts checks of adjacency and lengths, not eigenspectra; the independent replay does compute finite eigenspectra, but the proof, not either replay, establishes sharpness for all real b.

value.rationale: The half-translation equals the length of one Haar step and is a natural parameter rather than a fitted slice. The exact norm and conditioning on that lattice, discontinuous thresholds at noncritical densities, and the sharp constant determining instability near b=2 provide spectral information a frame-set criterion alone cannot give.
